label: 2026-08-20b_claude-opus-5-api-generic-v5_rep1

model.name: claude-fable-5
model.note: Evaluator is a Claude Code subagent; runtime model identity taken from the session environment (Fable 5, model id claude-fable-5). Temperature is the configured agent setting, not independently verifiable at runtime.

issues_detected.description: Internal tension on deidentification carried from sources: human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance states PHI was 'stripped ... using the Safe Harbor method' while is_deidentified.deidentification_details reports FAIRhub's 'NoDeIdentification' label and explains no active de-identification step was performed (identifiers were never collected). The record documents and reconciles the tension explicitly, but the two fields make superficially contradictory claims.
issues_detected.recommendation: Consider harmonizing the wording so both fields state 'verified free of HIPAA identifiers; Safe Harbor criteria used as the verification standard rather than as an active removal procedure'.

issues_detected.description: Sensitive-content claims disagree across sources: RO-Crate records personal sensitive information categories present (sensitive_elements_present: true) while the healthsheet states the public dataset contains no sensitive data. The record follows the RO-Crate and documents the disagreement in source_caveats.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change needed; the source_caveats resolution is appropriate. Upstream sources should be reconciled.

issues_detected.description: Institutional attribution is inconsistent across tier-1 sources (Washington University in St. Louis as managing organization/lead sponsor vs University of Washington as IRB, NIH RePORTER awardee, and PI department). The record surfaces this in source_caveats and data_governance.source_caveats rather than silently picking one.
issues_detected.recommendation: Flag to the AI-READI team for upstream metadata correction; the datasheet handles it correctly.

issues_detected.description: DOI prefix 10.60775 is not among the rubric's example registrars (PhysioNet, Zenodo, Harvard Dataverse) but is the DataCite prefix used by FAIRhub, and is consistent with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3. Treated as valid.

No software_and_tools field and no code repository links, despite the v3.0.0 processing chain being described as 'automated with custom steps'. Processing cannot be independently replicated from the datasheet alone.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add software_and_tools entries (or external_resources links) for the AI-READI processing/standardization pipelines, e.g. GitHub repositories, with versions.

issues_detected.description: ethical_reviews is unusually rich (IRB protocol number and dates, reliance agreements, named ethics group, Community Advisory Board, Native Biodata Consortium engagement) but contains no conflict-of-interest statement, positive or negative.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add an explicit conflicts-of-interest statement (even 'none declared by the sources') to ethical_reviews.

issues_detected.description: Character encoding is not stated for the text-based distribution formats (CSV, JSON, Markdown); only file formats and MIME types are given. Single data_topic slot on instances also cannot represent the multimodal topical breadth, a schema limit the record itself notes.
issues_detected.recommendation: State UTF-8/ASCII encoding for text formats; schema-level fix needed for multi-topic representation.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3 is format-valid and prefix-consistent with the FAIRhub publisher; version DOIs (fairhub.1, fairhub.2, fairhub.3) form a coherent versioned family matched one-to-one with release dates and participant counts (204 -> 1,067 -> 2,280).

NIH grant OT2OD032644 matches the NIH award pattern [Type OT2][Institute OD][Serial 032644] and is semantically consistent with the Bridge2AI Common Fund program named in description and funders; the record even flags the RePORTER application-ID discrepancy (10471118 vs 10885481).

Human-subjects logic fully consistent: involves_human_subjects=true is backed by IRB protocol STUDY00016228 with approval date, reliance agreements, written consent workflow with withdrawal mechanism, compensation (USD 200 with rationale), and at-risk population exclusions.

Privacy logic consistent and unusually candid: reidentification_risk is explicitly assessed (AI inference risk) and tied to concrete mitigations (two-tier access, custom license, static watermarking, sensor selection capturing no audio/video/GPS).

Temporal ordering is logical throughout: IRB approval 2022-12-20 precedes collection start 2023-07-19; collection window (to 2025-05-01) precedes issuance 2025-11-17; the three release dates are monotonic.

Split arithmetic checks out: 1,576 + 352 + 352 = 2,280 participants, matching instances.counts and the description; subset demographic counts sum correctly within splits (e.g. validation 88x4 race groups = 352, 176+176 sex = 352).
Subpopulation totals are internally consistent: race/ethnicity (380+545+519+836 = 2,280), sex (951+1,329 = 2,280), diabetes severity (776+560+686+258 = 2,280).

The record separates dataset-level facts from study-level facts (4,000-participant target, year-4 longitudinal arm, biorepository, controlled-access variant) and states the referent (v3.0.0 FAIRhub distribution) explicitly, avoiding the common conflation of study and release.

source_caveats blocks throughout distinguish attested values from inferred ones (e.g. keywords limited to those attested by FAIRhub/RO-Crate; consortium homepage used in place of a missing registry identifier, with the substitution named), which is exemplary provenance discipline.
ROR identifiers for affiliations, ORCID for the PI, RxNorm for medications, and HL7 confidentiality coding (2N) are all used in their correct semantic roles.

human_subjects.evidence: E1 description: 'multimodal data from 2,280 adult participants with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus'; E8 collection_mechanisms describe participant recruitment via REDCap and in-person study visits.

governance_restrictions.evidence: E2 regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; NIH GDS Policy compliance required.

datasets_shared_and_available.evidence: distribution_formats populated (DICOM, CSV, JSON, Markdown with MIME types); access_urls https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access; license grants reuse for research and commercial purposes.

software_tools_produced_as_output.evidence: external_resources reference only documentation sites (docs.aireadi.org, aireadi.org), not a code repository; description and purposes identify data, standards and best practices as outputs, not software. Gates E8 sub-elements 3-4 to not applicable.

data_collection_identified_and_shared.evidence: acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms richly populated; datasets-shared condition met.

publication_identified_and_shared.evidence: related_datasets include publication DOIs 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449; citation field present; datasets-shared condition met.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3
sub_elements.quality_note: DOI format valid (10.XXXXX/suffix). Prefix 10.60775 is FAIRhub's DataCite prefix, consistent with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and the landing page; versioned sibling DOIs (fairhub.1/.2) corroborate the namespace.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description spans version, cohort size (2,280), collection window, three sites, ten-plus modalities, recruitment balancing design, and the public/controlled-access distinction.
sub_elements.quality_note: Description far exceeds 200 chars and is semantically dense: specific counts, dates, sites, modalities, and the deliberate non-representativeness of the cohort are all stated.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam, Data Sharing, Exploratory Data Collection
sub_elements.quality_note: 9 relevant keywords covering condition, methods and modalities. source_caveats notes these are only the attested keywords; 'type 2 diabetes' and 'salutogenesis' were deliberately not invented — good provenance discipline at slight cost to searchability.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; 10 file_collections with ids, paths, file counts, byte sizes, and per-collection standards.
sub_elements.quality_note: Landing page plus an unusually complete hierarchical resource inventory (356,343 files, 3.8 TB, broken down per collection).

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and fairhub.1; is_described_by doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449; is_documented_by docs.aireadi.org.
sub_elements.quality_note: Typed relationships covering version lineage, describing publications, and documentation sites.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms: AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036) with storage, sublicensing, model-training and publication-figure limits; ip_restrictions: title and IP remain with Washington University in St. Louis.
sub_elements.quality_note: Exceptionally detailed and actionable: canonical license DOI (valid Zenodo prefix 10.5281), derivative-data and synthetic-data treatment, and separate-publisher-license requirement all stated.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions: confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; NIH GDS Policy security requirements; no FDA-regulated drug/device; HL7:2N coding noted; export-control question answered via license.
sub_elements.quality_note: Covers HIPAA status, NIH GDS, FDA status and confidentiality classification, and records what the sources do NOT state (export controls).

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats[DICOM].access_urls: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access; data_governance.access_review_process describes login via verified ID, self-attestation of intended use, and license acceptance.
sub_elements.quality_note: No standalone download_url field, but the platform access URL plus a step-by-step access process (PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired) is fully actionable.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: DICOM (application/dicom), CSV (text/csv), JSON (application/json), Markdown (text/markdown); per-collection formats WFDB, Open mHealth, NASA ASCII.
sub_elements.quality_note: Formats with MIME types, cross-referenced to per-collection standards and native/converted raw formats (.fda, .sdt, .FIT, .xml).

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets (6 typed entries); external_resources: docs.aireadi.org (CC-BY 4.0, publishes REDCap forms, IRB letter, consent form) and aireadi.org, with archival status and future guarantees addressed.
sub_elements.quality_note: Both fields populated; the external_resources entry even records the absence of archival snapshots and the Administration-review banner.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets-shared condition satisfied (distribution_formats + access URL + reuse-granting license), so sub-elements 1-4 are scored.

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.evidence: License 'grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the data and to create derivative works, for research and for commercial and non-commercial purposes'.
sub_elements.quality_note: Custom license rather than CC, but reuse scope, conditions and the disease-specific restriction on the public tier (data_use_permission: disease_specific_research) are explicit and consistent with consent_scope.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.evidence: WFDB for ECG, OMOP CDM for clinical/lab/survey, DICOM for all retinal imaging, Open mHealth for wearables/CGM, NASA ASCII for environmental data, CDS v0.1.1 layout.
sub_elements.quality_note: Every modality mapped to an established standard, including conversion of proprietary exports to DICOM. Character encoding is not explicitly stated (minor gap, noted as issue).

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: [CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT with FAIRscape profile 0.1.
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance stated at dataset level and per file_collection; includes the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard metadata file (dqd_omop.json, 3,500+ checks).

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.evidence: ~35 variables with variable_name, data_type, unit, measurement_technique, derivation where applicable, and laboratory reference ranges (e.g. hemoglobin_a1c 4.0-6.0%).
sub_elements.quality_note: Variable-level metadata spans labs, vitals, cognitive, visual, wearable and environmental domains; clinical significance noted per variable.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses (T2DM AI/ML research with examples; pipeline development against the mini subset); prohibited_uses: 7 specific prohibitions (no clinical decisions, no re-identification, no third-party model-vendor training, storage restrictions, watermark preservation, figure limits).
sub_elements.quality_note: Among the most complete use-guidance sections possible; other_tasks additionally scopes hypothesis-agnostic secondary use against the license restriction.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?
elements.applicability_note: Human-subjects condition satisfied via E1 description ('2,280 adult participants') and E8 collection_mechanisms (participant recruitment, consent workflow in REDCap); governance condition also satisfied via E2 (confidentiality_level: restricted). All five sub-elements applicable.

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: E1 description references 2,280 adult participants and clinical data collection; E8 collection_mechanisms describe recruitment and electronic consent; E2 regulatory_restrictions indicate governance constraints.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: UW IRB protocol STUDY00016228, initial approval 2022-12-20, annual renewal requirement, reliance agreements with UAB and UCSD IRBs; approval letter published with v3.0.0 documentation; named ethics group and Community Advisory Board.
sub_elements.quality_note: Consistency check passed: involves_human_subjects=true is fully backed by IRB detail. Also resolves the 'Washington University IRB' naming error in the RO-Crate with evidence.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified: method: HIPAA Safe Harbor; identifiers_removed: HIPAA Safe Harbor enumerated identifiers plus sex, race/ethnicity, medications; deidentification_details explains the 'NoDeIdentification' source label (no identifiers collected; verification rather than removal).
sub_elements.quality_note: Method appropriate for health data. The nuanced handling of the source's contradictory label is a strength, though the Safe-Harbor-as-method vs verification-only tension is flagged as a medium consistency issue.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy: anonymization method, five distinct privacy techniques (verified-ID gated access, custom license, static watermarking, two-tier dissemination, privacy-preserving device selection), data_linkage via study ID only, and explicit reidentification_risk (AI inference risk acknowledged).
sub_elements.quality_note: Explicit risk assessment tied to concrete mitigations; risk statement is consistent with future_use_impacts.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent: consent_obtained: true; written consent (electronic in REDCap or on paper); consent_scope covering biobanking, record abstraction and open-repository deposition; consent form published; withdrawal_mechanism with the already-shared-data limitation stated.
sub_elements.quality_note: Complete: type, scope, documentation location, withdrawal mechanism, plus collection_consents/notifications/revocations detail (staff read forms to participants with reading difficulty).

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations: at_risk_groups_included: false with explicit exclusions (minors, pregnancy, >85, prisoners not targeted) and transportation assistance; participant_compensation: USD 200 cash stipend, payment timing, non-pro-rating, and retention incentive parity for year-4 follow-up.
sub_elements.quality_note: Both halves documented with rationale; exclusion criteria consistent with known_limitations scope_limitation.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: race/ethnicity (Hispanic 380, Asian 545, Black 519, White 836), sex (951 M / 1,329 F), diabetes severity (776/560/686/258), mean age 60.8 +/- 11.3; controlled-access status of each variable stated.
sub_elements.quality_note: Counts sum exactly to 2,280 in all three breakdowns; subpopulation_elements_present flags correctly distinguish released vs withheld variables.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances: counts: 2280; subsets with is_data_split: true for train (1,576) / validation (352) / test (352); total_file_count: 356343; total_size_bytes: 3815969779678.
sub_elements.quality_note: Split arithmetic verified: 1,576 + 352 + 352 = 2,280. Per-split demographic and severity counts also internally consistent.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: is_tabular: false (correct for a multimodal imaging/waveform-dominated dataset); ~35 variables with types, units and measurement techniques; participants.tsv/json data-dictionary files listed in root metadata.
sub_elements.quality_note: is_tabular: false is semantically correct given DICOM/WFDB dominance; tabular components are still described via OMOP mapping.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances.data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:43 with note that T2DM is the primary subject and that ophthalmic imaging, mHealth, waveform and glucose-monitoring topics cannot be represented in the single-valued slot; description enumerates ten-plus health domains.
sub_elements.quality_note: Condition coverage clear; the record honestly names the schema's single-topic limitation rather than silently dropping information.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies (4: survey skips, device failure/misuse, image quality variation incl. FLIO positioning and cataract opacity, processing-chain data collisions); sampling_strategies with is_representative: false and why_not_representative; missing_data_documentation with patterns, causes and handling (no imputation; PI-reviewed removal).
sub_elements.quality_note: All three field groups populated with specific, modality-level detail; explicitly states no imputation was performed.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets-shared condition satisfied; all sub-elements scored.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.evidence: version: '3.0.0'; description and header consistently reference version 3.0.0.
sub_elements.quality_note: Semantic-versioning style, consistent everywhere it appears.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.evidence: version_access: latest_version_doi doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; per-version DOIs and release dates for 1.0.0/2.0.0/3.0.0; version dropdown at docs.aireadi.org; v2.0.0 marked no longer accessible with redirect notice.
sub_elements.quality_note: Documents both how to reach versions and which are no longer supported — including the honest statement that old versions will not be maintained.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.evidence: updates.update_details: participant count 1,067 -> 2,280, three imaging devices added, Snellen dropped for logMAR, recommended split introduced; CHANGELOG.md included in the release and mirrored at docs.aireadi.org.
sub_elements.quality_note: Concrete version-to-version deltas; no separate errata field, but the changelog mechanism covers it.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: 'Approximately once a year'; static-version release model explained; further versions expected while enrolment is ongoing.
sub_elements.quality_note: Frequency plus the release model (new versions rather than in-place updates) both stated.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: 11 entries mapping each raw export (REDCap, Philips .xml, Topcon .fda, Heidelberg .sdt, Dexcom .csv, Garmin .FIT, EHR abstraction) to its released standardized form; raw_sources explains why raw data are withheld.
sub_elements.quality_note: Full raw-to-released derivation chain per modality, including retention expectations for the raw tier.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: AI-ready ethically sourced T2DM dataset; salutogenesis research; pseudotime manifold analysis; establishing standards for AI/ML health data sharing. addressing_gaps: 4 specific gaps incl. a cited meta-epidemiological finding on racial/ethnic diversity in T2DM studies 2000-2020.
sub_elements.quality_note: Scientific rationale is specific and aligned with the Bridge2AI funding program named in funders — funding-purposes consistency check passes.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: pseudotime manifold analysis across four severity groups; multimodal ML model development; training/benchmarking with the 70/15/15 balanced splits.
sub_elements.quality_note: Concrete ML tasks tied to the dataset's actual structure (the supplied splits).

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: NIH (Bridge2AI Common Fund, 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project') and Research to Prevent Blindness; source_caveats distinguish FAIRhub-attested funding from publication-only mentions (P30DK035816, UL1TR003096).
sub_elements.quality_note: Primary mechanism and program named; secondary awards recorded with their weaker attestation level rather than promoted or dropped.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: 'NIH award number OT2OD032644, made through the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program'; grant id is the NIH RePORTER project URI.
sub_elements.quality_note: Semantic check passed: OT2OD032644 matches the NIH pattern (activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032644) and OT2/OD is exactly the Common Fund Other Transaction mechanism used by Bridge2AI. The RePORTER application-ID discrepancy (10471118 vs 10885481) is flagged in-source.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: AI-READI Consortium with PI Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648) and 8 ROR-identified affiliated institutions; maintainers and data_collectors sections credit site staff roles.
sub_elements.quality_note: Registry identifiers used correctly (ROR, ORCID); source_caveats transparently notes the consortium lacks a registry ID and that individual members are not recorded as creators by FAIRhub.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?
elements.applicability_note: Data-collection-identified and datasets-shared conditions satisfied (sub-elements 1-2, 5 scored). Software-tools condition NOT satisfied: external_resources reference only documentation sites, and description/purposes identify data and standards, not software, as outputs — sub-elements 3-4 set to applicable: false per the gating rule.

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms populated; distribution_formats and access URL establish sharing.
sub_elements.evidence: 19 collection_mechanisms entries with device make/model/manufacturer, acquisition protocols (e.g. Spectralis 20x20 512-line macular OCTA; Dexcom G6 5-minute interstitial glucose, participant-masked; Mars chart at 40-59 cm, 60-120 cd/m2), and export formats.
sub_elements.quality_note: Device-level protocol detail sufficient for replication assessment; visit duration (2.5-4 h) and 10-day home-monitoring design included.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods distinguish directly-observed vs participant-reported data with validation flags (medication self-reports cross-checked against physical medications); raw_data_sources enumerate every pre-processing source and format.
sub_elements.quality_note: Observation/report/validation flags used correctly; site-specific protocol variation (e.g. marijuana question omitted in Alabama for legal reasons) captured.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: external_resources (E10) contain documentation sites only, no code repository; E1 description and E7 purposes identify the dataset, standards and best practices as outputs, not software. Per the anti-circular rule this determination rests on E10/E1/E7 fields, not on E8's own fields.
sub_elements.evidence: Reported but not scored: preprocessing_strategies (OMOP/DICOM/WFDB/Open mHealth mapping, CDS assembly, watermarking, sensitive-variable withholding), cleaning_strategies (REDCap range checks, PI-approved editing), and missing_data handling are all richly documented; no labeling/annotation was performed by design (label: false, hypothesis-agnostic).
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from denominator per the software-tools gating condition. Content quality is high and would merit a passing score were the condition met.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same external evidence as sub-element 3: no code repository in external_resources; software not identified as an output in description/purposes.
sub_elements.evidence: Reported but not scored: no software_and_tools field is present. The processing chain is described as 'automated with custom steps' but no pipeline software, versions or repositories are named.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from denominator, but flagged as the record's main reproducibility gap — see issues_detected and recommendations.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to/conforms_to_standard (7 standards); external_resources: docs.aireadi.org (CC-BY 4.0) publishing REDCap forms, IRB letter and consent form; describing publications in related_datasets (Nature Metabolism, BMJ Open).
sub_elements.quality_note: Standards, documentation and publications all referenced with archival status assessed.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: 6 typed limitations (representativeness, coverage, scope, temporal, methodological, integration) each with limitation_description, scope_impact and, where available, recommended_mitigation.
sub_elements.quality_note: Structured, typed, and actionable — e.g. cross-sectional design forces pseudotime rather than longitudinal approaches; multi-device non-interchangeability with a device-stratification mitigation.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: bias_type values selection_bias, sampling_bias, representation_bias with descriptions and mitigation strategies; future_use_impacts covers re-identification risk and generalizability constraints on downstream use.
sub_elements.quality_note: Enum-style bias typing with substantive content, including the historically grounded discussion of recruitment difficulty for Black, Hispanic and Asian participants and the English-language requirement's own bias effect.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: survey skips, wearable battery/technical failures, image quality degradation (handheld undilated Optomed, FLIO after light exposure, cataract opacity), and processing-chain data collisions with data loss.
sub_elements.quality_note: Specific, modality-attributed quality issues rather than boilerplate.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present: true with the RO-Crate category list and the controlled-access holding of zip code, sex, race, ethnicity, genetics, past records, traffic reports; content_warnings: content_warnings_present: false with the healthsheet's justification.
sub_elements.quality_note: Both fields populated with correct polarity; the RO-Crate vs healthsheet disagreement on 'sensitive' is surfaced in source_caveats (low-severity consistency warning).

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: IRB protocol/dates/renewal, named ethics group (Nebeker, Mathews, Ferryman, Evans), Native Biodata Consortium co-learning engagement, 11-member Community Advisory Board reflecting sample diversity.
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethical review documentation is exceptional; however no conflict-of-interest statement (positive or negative) appears anywhere — recorded as a low-severity completeness issue.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets-shared condition satisfied; publication condition for sub-element 2 satisfied via publication DOIs in related_datasets. All sub-elements scored.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: https://fairhub.io/; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; FAIRhub is the Bridge2AI data-sharing platform, hosted on Microsoft Azure per maintainers.
sub_elements.quality_note: Platform, landing page and DOI namespace are mutually consistent.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: related_datasets include describing publications doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449; datasets-shared condition met.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3'
sub_elements.quality_note: Complete recommended citation in DataCite style with version and resolvable DOI; both describing publications have valid DOI prefixes (Nature 10.1038, BMJ 10.1136).

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.evidence: OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB, Open mHealth, NASA ESDS, CDS v0.1.1, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT/FAIRscape profile, plus conforms_to_schema for the Bridge2AI data-sheets schema.
sub_elements.quality_note: Broadest community-standards conformance in the Bridge2AI corpus; standards named at both dataset and collection level.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: docs.aireadi.org (version-specific domain documentation, AI-readiness discussion, citation instructions) and aireadi.org (team and contact); page on FAIRhub.
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation ecosystem well linked; the note about the Administration-review banner on both sites is unusual and useful situational awareness for users.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of (fairhub.2, fairhub.1), is_described_by (two publication DOIs), is_documented_by (two documentation sites) — 6 typed entries.
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationship types used semantically correctly, distinguishing version lineage from description and documentation.

strengths: Provenance discipline is exemplary: source_caveats blocks throughout distinguish attested from inferred values, surface source contradictions (WashU vs UW attribution, healthsheet vs RO-Crate sensitivity claims, 'NoDeIdentification' label, RePORTER application-ID mismatch) and state which reading was followed and why, rather than silently resolving or inventing.

Complete and internally consistent quantitative composition: participant counts, split sizes and all three subpopulation breakdowns sum exactly to 2,280; file counts and byte sizes are given per collection down to a 356,343-file, 3.8 TB total.

Ethics and privacy documentation is fully cross-consistent: IRB protocol number and dates, reliance agreements, written consent with published form and withdrawal mechanism, explicit re-identification risk assessment tied to five concrete mitigations (verified-ID access, custom license, watermarking, two-tier dissemination, privacy-preserving device selection), and compensation with rationale.

Standards conformance is stated at both dataset and per-collection level across seven community standards (OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB, Open mHealth, NASA ESDS, CDS, RO-Crate), with the raw-to-released format derivation chain documented for every modality.

Use guidance is unusually actionable: seven specific license prohibitions, the disease-specific restriction on the public tier, third-party model-vendor rules, and the mini-subset pathway for pipeline development.
weaknesses: No software or code repository references: software_and_tools is absent and external_resources link only to documentation sites, despite a processing chain described as 'automated with custom steps' — the main reproducibility gap (E8 sub-elements 3-4 were gated to N/A by the rubric, but the gap is real).

Residual internal tension on deidentification: Safe Harbor is named as the method in two places while deidentification_details explains no active de-identification step occurred; the reconciliation is documented but the surface-level fields still disagree.

No conflict-of-interest statement in ethical_reviews, and no explicit character-encoding declaration for the text-based distribution formats; the single-valued data_topic slot cannot represent the dataset's multimodal topical breadth (a schema limit the record itself flags).
recommendations: Add software_and_tools entries (pipeline names, versions, repository URLs) for the OMOP mapping, DICOM conversion, Open mHealth transformation and CDS assembly steps; if AI-READI publishes processing code on GitHub, link it in external_resources.

Harmonize the deidentification wording: state in human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance and is_deidentified.method that Safe Harbor criteria were used as a verification standard (no identifiers collected) rather than as an active removal procedure, matching deidentification_details.

Add an explicit conflicts-of-interest statement to ethical_reviews (even 'none declared in the sources'), and declare character encoding (e.g. UTF-8) alongside the text/csv, application/json and text/markdown media types.
Consider adding a top-level download_url mirroring https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access, and extending access_urls beyond the DICOM entry to all four distribution formats.
Propose a schema change to allow multivalued data_topic on instances so the ophthalmic imaging, mHealth, waveform and glucose-monitoring topics can be represented alongside T2DM.
